prompt.brief: Design an evidence-driven root-cause analysis platform that correlates metrics, logs, traces, topology, deployments, and incidents to rank likely causes while preserving operator trust and raw evidence.
successSignals: Define incident windows, signal identity, service topology, deployment/change context, hypotheses, evidence links, confidence, and analyst feedback.
Correlate temporal and dependency relationships without claiming causality from correlation; handle missing telemetry, topology drift, and noisy signals.
Separate telemetry ingestion from feature/graph construction, interactive investigation, offline learning, and immutable incident evidence.
Explain privacy, tenant isolation, feedback bias, replay, failure recovery, observability, and a deterministic evidence-only fallback.

functional: Ingest and normalize signals, detect incident boundaries, build topology context, rank root-cause hypotheses, and link supporting evidence.
Provide investigation timelines, deployment correlation, blast-radius views, confidence/limitations, operator annotations, and incident exports.
Support replay, topology updates, signal deletion, model/version rollback, access controls, and recovery after delayed or missing telemetry.
nonFunctional: Produce an initial evidence-backed hypothesis within five minutes while labeling uncertainty and never hiding the raw incident signals.
Analyze 100k incidents per day across 50k services without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Evidence-driven root-cause analysis platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Evidence-driven root-cause analysis platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Evidence-driven root-cause analysis platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Evidence-driven root-cause analysis platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Evidence-driven root-cause analysis platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Evidence-driven root-cause analysis platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Evidence-driven root-cause analysis platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Evidence-driven root-cause analysis platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Evidence-driven root-cause analysis platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
